title: Plancherel Measure and Asymptotic Young Diagrams

items.title: The Plancherel measure on the partitions of $n$
items.statement: For every integer $n\ge0$ let $Y_n$ be the set of partitions $\lambda\vdash n$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]), a finite set, and put $f^\lambda:=\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda$, the dimension of the complex Specht module, so that $f^\lambda$ equals the number of standard $\lambda$-tableaux ([[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]], [[thm-hook-length-formula]]). The **Plancherel measure of order $n$** is the function $$P_n(\lambda):=\frac{(f^\lambda)^2}{n!},\qquad \lambda\in Y_n,$$ with $n!$ the factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]] and the conventions $0!=1$ and $f^\varnothing=1$, so that $P_0(\varnothing)=1$. Each $P_n(\lambda)$ is a nonnegative real number and $P_n$ is a function on the finite set $Y_n$.
items.strategy: Define the weights and record the elementary well-definedness facts. $Y_n$ is finite: a partition of $n$ has at most $n$ parts and every part is at most $n$. $f^\lambda$ is a positive integer, being the cardinality of the standard-polytabloid basis, and the hook-length formula computes it as $n!/\prod h(x)$. Finally $n!>0$, so each $P_n(\lambda)$ is a well-defined nonnegative real. No choice principle is used; every quantity is finite. Normalization is not asserted here: it is a separate proposition.

items.title: The Plancherel weights sum to one
items.statement:
For every $n\ge0$,
$$\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}P_n(\lambda)=\frac{1}{n!}\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}(f^\lambda)^2=1.$$
Hence $P_n$ is a probability distribution on the finite set $Y_n$ ([[def-finite-probability-space-and-event]]): the weights are nonnegative and sum to one. In particular $\dim_{\mathbb C}\mathbb C[S_n]=n!=\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}(f^\lambda)^2$ is obtained in two independent ways.
items.strategy: Complex characteristic zero and n!>0 meet the regular-decomposition theorem's hypotheses; the complete irredundant Specht list and polytabloid basis turn its dimension sum into sum (f^lambda)^2=n!. The independent RSK/tableau-square supplier has exactly the same identity for all n>=0. Dividing by n! gives nonnegative normalized weights; n=0 is the one-point space of weight 1. The reader correctly removed the false assertion that primes divide no positive integer; no claim change or new item edit is needed. IO §5 p.25 gives the Burnside normalization.

items.title: The RSK shape of a uniform random permutation has the Plancherel law
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and let $\sigma$ be uniformly distributed on $S_n$ ([[def-uniform-finite-probability-space]]). Let $\operatorname{sh}(\sigma)\vdash n$ be the common shape of the Robinson-Schensted pair $(P(\sigma),Q(\sigma))$ ([[thm-robinson-schensted-correspondence]]). Then $\operatorname{sh}$ is a random element with values in the finite measurable space $(Y_n,2^{Y_n})$ ([[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]) and for every $\lambda\vdash n$
$$\mathbb P\bigl(\operatorname{sh}(\sigma)=\lambda\bigr)=\frac{(f^\lambda)^2}{n!}=P_n(\lambda).$$
In particular the uniform distribution on $S_n$ pushes forward to the Plancherel measure of order $n$, and the length of a longest increasing subsequence of $\sigma$ has the same law as the first row length of a Plancherel-random diagram.
items.strategy: The current Robinson–Schensted Statement is a bijection for all n>=0 onto ordered pairs of standard tableaux of the same shape. For the theorem's n>=1 the fibre has (f^lambda)^2 elements and each permutation has weight 1/n!. The finite shape map is measurable into (Y_n,2^Y_n), so its pushforward is exactly P_n. The real-valued random-variable definition is now reserved for real functions or encodings, resolving the reader's typing defect. Schensted's exact Statement identifies first-row length with LIS pointwise, giving the final equality of laws. n=1 has a one-point fibre; no choice is used. IO §5 p.25 gives the same weights; the result follows completely from the local suppliers.

items.title: Continual diagrams, Russian profiles, and the $\sqrt n$-scaling of a Young diagram
items.statement:
A **continual diagram** is a function $\omega:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ such that $|\omega(x)-\omega(y)|\le|x-y|$ for all real $x,y$ (the Lipschitz condition) and $\omega(x)=|x|$ for all sufficiently large $|x|$; the set of continual diagrams is denoted $D_0$. For $\omega\in D_0$ set
$$\sigma_\omega(x):=\tfrac12\bigl(\omega(x)-|x|\bigr).$$
Since $\omega$ agrees with $|\cdot|$ outside a compact set, $\sigma_\omega$ is compactly supported; and $\sigma_\omega$ is 1-Lipschitz, because $|\sigma_\omega(x)-\sigma_\omega(y)|=\tfrac12|\omega(x)-\omega(y)-(|x|-|y|)|\le\tfrac12(|x-y|+|x-y|)$ by the Lipschitz bound and $\bigl||x|-|y|\bigr|\le|x-y|$: the latter follows by applying [[lem-of-triangle-inequality]] to $x=(x-y)+y$ and to $y=(y-x)+x$, with [[lem-of-abs-value]]. For $s>0$ define the **$s$-scaling** $\omega_s(x):=s^{-1}\omega(sx)$. Then $\omega_s\in D_0$, and
$$\sigma_{\omega_s}(x)=s^{-1}\sigma_\omega(sx),\qquad x\in\mathbb R,$$
directly from the definition, so scaling preserves the Lipschitz constant.

The empty partition has profile $\varnothing(x):=|x|$. Every nonempty $\lambda\vdash n$ determines a continual diagram $\lambda(\cdot)\in D_0$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]). Regard the boxes of $[\lambda]$ as the unit squares $[i-1,i]\times[j-1,j]$, $1\le i\le k$, $1\le j\le\lambda_i$, in the plane with coordinates $(r,s)$, and rotate by $x=s-r$, $y=r+s$. The outer staircase of the image, extended by the two axis rays, is the graph of a continuous piecewise linear function $y=\lambda(x)$, with $\lambda'(x)=\pm1$ at every point where the derivative exists ([[def-derivative]]): each horizontal or vertical unit step of the boundary staircase becomes a unit step of slope $\mp1$ under the linear map $(r,s)\mapsto(s-r,r+s)$, and the graph is read from the outer corner at $x=-\lambda'_1$ to the corner at $x=\lambda_1$. Outside these corners the boundary follows the axis strip, so
$$\lambda(x)=|x|\quad\text{for }x\ge\lambda_1\quad\text{and for }x\le-\lambda'_1,$$
the extreme corners being the end of the first row and the bottom of the first column. Hence $\lambda(\cdot)\in D_0$ and the support of $\sigma_\lambda$ is contained in $[-\lambda'_1,\lambda_1]$. The **area identity**, also valid for the empty profile, holds:
$$\tfrac12\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\lambda(x)-|x|\bigr)dx=n,$$
because the compact region $\{(x,y):-\lambda\prime_1\le x\le\lambda_1,\ |x|\le y\le\lambda(x)\}$ is exactly the image under the invertible linear map $T(r,s):=(s-r,r+s)$, of determinant $-2$, of the union $[\lambda]$ of the $n$ unit squares, and the image of a Jordan-measurable compact set of area $n$ has area $|\det T|\cdot n=2n$ ([[thm-change-of-variables-for-compact-jordan-sets]], applied with $f\equiv1$); the region is the area under the continuous piecewise linear function $\lambda(x)-|x|\ge0$ over the compact interval $[-\lambda'_1,\lambda_1]$, which is its Riemann-Darboux integral ([[def-darboux-integral]]).

The **$\sqrt n$-scaled profile** of $\lambda\vdash n$, $n\ge1$, is
$$\bar\lambda(x):=n^{-1/2}\lambda\bigl(n^{1/2}x\bigr)=\lambda_{n^{1/2}}(x),\qquad x\in\mathbb R,$$
the $\sqrt n$-scaling of the preceding paragraph. Thus $\bar\lambda\in D_0$, $\bar\lambda(x)=|x|$ for $|x|\ge\max(\lambda_1,\lambda'_1)/\sqrt n$, and $\sigma_{\bar\lambda}(x)=n^{-1/2}\sigma_\lambda(n^{1/2}x)$; the area identity scales to $\tfrac12\int_{\mathbb R}(\bar\lambda(x)-|x|)dx=1$. The probability distribution with which $\lambda$ is drawn in this batch is the Plancherel measure of [[def-plancherel-measure-on-partitions]]. No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: The current definition uses the outer staircase with axis rays, giving slopes ±1 and support in [-lambda'_1,lambda_1]; its empty profile is |x|. The linear map (r,s)->(s-r,r+s) has determinant -2, so the published compact-Jordan change-of-variables theorem gives transformed area 2n for the n-square union; integrating half the excess gives n. At the empty profile the excess is identically zero; normalization is only defined for n>=1. Scaling both axes by sqrt(n) gives area 1 for sigma and preserves the Lipschitz constant. The inverse-triangle estimate proves sigma is 1-Lipschitz. Reader repairs to the compact area region and probability terminology are retained. IO introduction p.2, Definitions 2.1/2.3 pp.9–10 and scaling pp.13–14 match these conventions.

items.title: The Logan-Shepp-Vershik-Kerov limit profile $\Omega$
items.statement:
Define the function $\Omega:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by
$$\Omega(x)=\frac2\pi\Bigl(x\arcsin\frac x2+\sqrt{4-x^2}\Bigr)\quad(|x|\le2),\qquad \Omega(x)=|x|\quad(|x|\ge2).$$ Then $\Omega$ is even, the two formulas agree at $x=\pm2$ with common value $2$, $\Omega$ is continuous on $\mathbb R$, continuously differentiable there with
$$\Omega'(x)=\frac2\pi\arcsin\frac x2\ (|x|<2),\qquad \Omega'(x)=\operatorname{sgn}x\ (|x|>2),$$
$|\Omega'(x)|<1$ for $|x|<2$, and $\Omega$ is $C^\infty$ on $(-2,2)$ with $\Omega''(x)=\frac2\pi(4-x^2)^{-1/2}$ there. Consequently $\Omega\in D_0$ and $\Omega$ is $1$-Lipschitz, with equality of the two one-sided derivatives at $x=\pm2$.
items.strategy: Evaluate both branches at $\pm2$: $\frac2\pi(\pm2\arcsin(\pm1)+0)=\pm2$ for $x=\pm2$ since $\arcsin(\pm1)=\pm\pi/2$, agreeing with $|x|=2$. On $(-2,2)$ differentiate the arcsine branch: $\frac{d}{dx}\arcsin(x/2)=(1-(x/2)^2)^{-1/2}/2$ by the inverse-function derivative applied to sine ([[thm-derivative-of-an-inverse]], [[thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives]]) and the chain rule; the $\sqrt{4-x^2}$ term contributes $-\frac{x}{\sqrt{4-x^2}}$, so $\Omega'(x)=\frac2\pi\arcsin(x/2)$; as $x\to2^-$ this tends to $\frac2\pi\cdot\frac\pi2=1$, matching $\operatorname{sgn}x=1$ for $x>2$, and similarly at $-2$; hence $\Omega$ is $C^1$ on $\mathbb R$. Since $|\arcsin y|<\pi/2$ for $|y|<1$, $|\Omega'|<1$ inside and $|\Omega'|=1$ outside, so the mean value theorem gives the $1$-Lipschitz bound on each side and, by continuity of $\Omega'$, on $\mathbb R$. Evenness is immediate from the evenness of $|x|$ and of $x\mapsto x\arcsin(x/2)+\sqrt{4-x^2}$. This is exactly the profile and constants of the source.

items.title: The RSK union bound localizes Plancherel profiles
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$, let $\sigma$ be uniform on $S_n$ and let $\lambda=\operatorname{sh}(\sigma)\vdash n$. For every integer $L$ with $1\le L\le n$,
$$\mathbb P(\lambda_1\ge L)\le\frac{\binom nL}{L!}\le\Bigl(\frac{e^2n}{L^2}\Bigr)^{L},$$
and the same two inequalities hold for $\lambda'_1$. Consequently, for every constant $C>e$ there is $n_0$ such that for all $n\ge n_0$
$$\mathbb P\bigl(\lambda_1\le C\sqrt n\ \text{ and }\ \lambda'_1\le C\sqrt n\bigr)\ge1-2\Bigl(\frac{e^2}{C^2}\Bigr)^{\lfloor C\sqrt n\rfloor-1}\longrightarrow1,$$
and on the event in question the function $x\mapsto\bar\lambda(x)-|x|$ is supported in the fixed compact interval $[-C,C]$.
items.strategy: For each L-subset of positions exactly n!/L! permutations have increasing relative order, so the union bound gives binom(n,L)/L!; word reversal gives the same decreasing bound. The current factorial-formula supplier is thm-binomial-closed-formula rather than its definition. Its inequality and the exponential-series term e^L>=L^L/L! yield (e^2 n/L^2)^L. With L_n=floor(C sqrt(n))+1, eventually L_n<=n and L_n>C sqrt(n); q=e^2/C^2 is in (0,1), so q^(L_n)<=q^(floor(C sqrt(n))-1) tends to zero. The profile support supplier then gives [-C,C]. L=1 and L=n pose no denominator problem. The informal word random variable in Given means the finite random element already typed precisely in the RSK supplier; no real-valued conclusion is asserted here. Reader citation repair is sound and retained. IO Lemma 5.6 p.28 asks only for fixed compact localization, which this local proof supplies without Hammersley.

items.title: Finitely many polynomial moments control the uniform distance on bounded Lipschitz profiles
items.statement:
Fix $I=[a,b]$ with $a\le b$ and let $\Sigma_I$ be the set of real functions $\sigma$ with support in $I$ satisfying $|\sigma(x)-\sigma(y)|\le|x-y|$ for all $x,y$. Then for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exist $K\in\mathbb N$ and $\delta>0$ such that every $\sigma\in\Sigma_I$ with
$$\Bigl|\int_{\mathbb R}\sigma(x)x^k\,dx\Bigr|\le\delta\qquad(k=0,1,\dots,K)$$
satisfies $\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}|\sigma(x)|\le\varepsilon$. Consequently, if $(\sigma_n)\subseteq\Sigma_I$ and $\int_{\mathbb R}\sigma_n(x)x^k\,dx\to0$ for every $k\ge0$, then $\sigma_n\to0$ uniformly on $\mathbb R$; equivalently, on $\Sigma_I$ the topology of all polynomial moments coincides with the topology of uniform convergence.
items.strategy: Read every step and the exact Weierstrass, continuity/integrability, integral linearity and monotonicity Statements. Vanishing outside [a,b] forces zero endpoints and a common height bound; a=b forces the zero function. Each triangular bump has mass 1 and detects values above eta, polynomial approximation controls its integral uniformly, and the finite mesh yields K and delta depending only on the interval and tolerance. For topology at arbitrary tau, (sigma-tau)/2 has Lipschitz constant at most 1; the reverse estimate bounds every moment by the sup norm. Both topology directions are therefore established without a sequential-closure assumption. F5's nonstrict absolute-value equivalence follows immediately from the definition although the named lemma states its strict version. The reader's continuous-test and topology corrections are sound and retained. IO Lemma 5.7 pp.28–29 is supporting context; the polynomial replacement is supplied locally.

items.title: Shifted character observables $p_\rho^\#$ and profile moments $\tilde p_k$
items.statement:
**(a) Shifted character observables.** For a partition $\rho\vdash r$ ([[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]]) and $\lambda\vdash n$ set
$$p_\rho^\#(\lambda):=\begin{cases}n^{\downarrow r}\dfrac{\chi^\lambda_{\rho\cup1^{n-r}}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda},&n\ge r,\\[4pt]0,&n<r,\end{cases}$$
where $n^{\downarrow r}=n(n-1)\cdots(n-r+1)$ is the falling factorial of [[def-factorial-and-falling-factorial]], $\rho\cup1^{n-r}=(\rho,1,\dots,1)\vdash n$ is the padded partition, $\chi^\lambda$ is the complex irreducible character of $S_n$ indexed by $\lambda$, and $\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda=\chi^\lambda_{(1^n)}=f^\lambda>0$ by [[thm-standard-polytabloid-basis]]. Character values are the power-sum coefficients, $\chi^\lambda(\mu)=\langle s_\lambda,p_\mu\rangle$ for $\mu\vdash n$ ([[cor-irreducible-symmetric-group-character-values-are-power-sum-coefficients]]). For $n\ge r$ the quotient is a finite real number: a permutation and its inverse have the same cycle type and are conjugate (reverse the order within each cycle), while a complex character satisfies $\chi(g^{-1})=\overline{\chi(g)}$ and is constant on conjugacy classes ([[prop-basic-value-properties-of-a-complex-character]]). Therefore $\chi(g)=\overline{\chi(g)}$. The definition for $n<r$ is consistent with $n^{\downarrow r}=0$: in particular
$$p_1^\#(\lambda)=n^{\downarrow1}\frac{\chi^\lambda_{(1^n)}}{\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda}=n\frac{f^\lambda}{f^\lambda}=n\qquad(\lambda\vdash n,\ n\ge1).$$

**(b) Profile moments.** For $\omega\in D_0$ with profile $\sigma_\omega=\frac12(\omega-|x|)$ ([[def-russian-profile-and-sqrt-n-scaling-of-a-young-diagram]]) and $k\ge2$ define the **profile moment**
$$\tilde p_k[\omega]:=k(k-1)\int_{\mathbb R}x^{k-2}\sigma_\omega(x)\,dx,\qquad\tilde p_1[\omega]:=0 .$$
The integrand is continuous, since $\sigma_\omega$ is Lipschitz, and compactly supported. Its integral is the Riemann integral over any compact interval containing its support, so it exists and is finite by [[thm-continuous-implies-integrable]]. If in addition $\omega$ is piecewise linear with finitely many corners, $\sigma_\omega$ is continuous, compactly supported and piecewise $C^1$, and applying integration by parts on each linear piece and summing (the boundary terms cancel, since $\sigma_\omega$ vanishes at the ends and its values at the interior corners enter twice with opposite signs) gives
$$\tilde p_k[\omega]=-k\int_{\mathbb R}x^{k-1}\sigma_\omega'(x)\,dx\qquad(k\ge2),$$
in agreement with the source's formula (2.2), where $\sigma_\omega'$ exists except at the finitely many corners; this is the form used for the Young-diagram profiles of this page. The convention $\tilde p_1=0$ is the source's.

**(c) Scaling.** For every $s>0$ and $k\ge2$, the substitution $y=sx$ ([[thm-monotone-change-of-variable-for-riemann-integrals]], applied on a compact interval containing the support) in the definition of the $s$-scaling $\omega_s(x)=s^{-1}\omega(sx)$ gives
$$\tilde p_k[\omega_s]=k(k-1)\int_{\mathbb R}x^{k-2}\tfrac12\bigl(s^{-1}\omega(sx)-|x|\bigr)dx=k(k-1)s^{-k}\int_{\mathbb R}y^{k-2}\sigma_\omega(y)\,dy=s^{-k}\tilde p_k[\omega],$$
because $\frac12(s^{-1}|sx|-|x|)=0$; hence for $\lambda\vdash n$, $n\ge1$, the $\sqrt n$-scaled profile $\bar\lambda$ of [[def-russian-profile-and-sqrt-n-scaling-of-a-young-diagram]] satisfies
$$\tilde p_k[\bar\lambda]=n^{-k/2}\tilde p_k[\lambda(\cdot)].$$
No choice principle is used.
items.strategy: For n>=r the padded cycle type has size n and dim S^lambda=f^lambda>0; inverse conjugacy of symmetric-group permutations and the exact complex-character identity make the quotient real. The n<r branch is zero without attempting an undefined character, and rho empty gives p_empty^#=1 including n=0. For each continual diagram the profile integrand is continuous with compact support, so the stated Riemann integral exists; on finitely many linear pieces integration by parts has cancelling endpoint terms. The positive affine substitution gives s^(-k), so sqrt(n) scaling is understood only for n>=1 as its supplier specifies. tilde p_1=0 and no tilde p_0 is used. Reader repairs to real-valuedness, integrability and substitution citation are retained. IO Definitions 3.1/4.1 pp.15/19, Proposition 2.2 p.10 and scaling pp.13–14 match exactly.

items.title: Joint convergence in distribution and the normalized cycle-character observables
items.statement:
Fix an integer $N\ge2$. For $n\ge1$ and $2\le k\le N$ define the real random variable
$$\eta_k^{(n)}(\lambda):=\frac{p_k^\#(\lambda)}{\sqrt k\,n^{k/2}},\qquad\lambda\vdash n,$$
on the finite probability space $(Y_n,P_n)$ of [[def-plancherel-measure-on-partitions]], normalized by [[prop-plancherel-weights-sum-to-one]], and let $\eta^{(n)}:=(\eta_2^{(n)},\dots,\eta_N^{(n)})$ be the corresponding $\mathbb R^{N-1}$-valued random element. **Joint convergence in distribution** of such vectors means convergence in distribution of random elements in the sense of [[def-convergence-in-distribution-of-random-elements]], that is, weak convergence of their laws ([[def-law-or-distribution-of-a-random-element]]) against every bounded continuous function on $\mathbb R^{N-1}$. The **standard Gaussian target law** is $N_{N-1}(0,I_{N-1})$ ([[def-multivariate-normal-law]]), the law of a vector with independent standard normal coordinates; under AC this law exists. For independent standard Gaussian variables $\xi_k$, $2\le k\le N$, the target law for the normalized vector $\eta^{(n)}$ is that of $(\xi_2,\dots,\xi_N)$. The unnormalized observables $p_k^\#/n^{k/2}$ instead have target coordinates $\zeta_k:=\sqrt{k}\,\xi_k$, independent centered Gaussians of variance $k$.
items.strategy: Definitional item. It fixes the normalization $\eta_k^{(n)}=p_k^\#/(\sqrt k\,n^{k/2})$, the finite-dimensional joint-convergence convention, and the target product-Gaussian law. The normalization is choice-free; existence of the target law is the AC-dependent input of [[def-multivariate-normal-law]] and is used only to name the limit. No convergence is asserted here.

items.title: The shifted character observables form a basis of $A$, with the Kerov weight filtration
items.statement:
Let $A$ be the commutative $\mathbb R$-algebra of functions on $D_0$ generated by the profile moments $\tilde p_2,\tilde p_3,\dots$ of [[def-shifted-character-observables-and-profile-moments]], so $A=\mathbb R[\tilde p_2,\tilde p_3,\dots]$ as a polynomial algebra, and regard its elements as functions on Young diagrams through $\lambda\mapsto\lambda(\cdot)$. Let $p_\rho^\#$ be the shifted character observables of the same item, $|\rho|_1=|\rho|+m_1(\rho)$ and $\operatorname{wt}(\tilde p_k):=k$. Then:

(i) every function $p_\rho^\#$ belongs to $A$, and the family $\{p_\rho^\#\}_\rho$ is a linear basis of $A$;

(ii) $\deg_1(p_\rho^\#):=|\rho|_1$ defines an algebra filtration: if $p_\sigma^\#p_\tau^\#=\sum_\rho f^\rho_{\sigma\tau}p_\rho^\#$ then $f^\rho_{\sigma\tau}\ne0$ implies $\deg_1(p_\rho^\#)\le\deg_1(p_\sigma^\#)+\deg_1(p_\tau^\#)$; moreover the weights $\operatorname{wt}(p_\rho^\#):=|\rho|+\ell(\rho)$ define an algebra filtration which dominates the first one, $\deg_1(f)\le\operatorname{wt}(f)$ for every $f\in A$, and which is the weight filtration generated by $\operatorname{wt}(\tilde p_k)=k$;

(iii) the top term with respect to the weight filtration is unique with coefficient one:
$$p_\sigma^\#p_\tau^\#=p_{\sigma\cup\tau}^\#+\langle\text{terms of strictly smaller weight}\rangle,$$
where $\sigma\cup\tau$ is the partition obtained by uniting all parts of $\sigma$ and $\tau$.

In particular, the monomials in $\tilde p_2,\tilde p_3,\dots$ (including $1$) and the family $\{p_\rho^\#\}$ are two linear bases of the same algebra. The source's claim "$|\rho|_N=|\rho|+\ell(\rho)$ filtration equals the weight filtration" is the corresponding statement for $J=\mathbb N$, not for $J=\{1\}$.

items.title: Shifted character products: exact for $p_1^\#$ and leading terms for $p_k^\#$
items.statement:
For every partition $\sigma$:

(i) (exact, all orders) $p_\sigma^\#p_1^\#=p_{\sigma\cup1}^\#+|\sigma|\,p_\sigma^\#$;

(ii) for every $k\ge2$,
$$p_\sigma^\#p_k^\#=p_{\sigma\cup k}^\#+\begin{cases}k\,m_k(\sigma)\,p_{(\sigma\setminus k)\cup1^k}^\#, & m_k(\sigma)\ge1,\\[1pt]0,&m_k(\sigma)=0,\end{cases}+\langle\text{terms of strictly smaller }\deg_1\rangle,$$
where $\sigma\setminus k$ removes one part equal to $k$.

In particular, for $m\ge1$, $k\ge2$,
$$p_{(k^m)}^\#p_k^\#=p_{(k^{m+1})}^\#+km\,p_{(k^{m-1},1^k)}^\#+\langle\text{lower }\deg_1\text{ terms}\rangle,$$
which is the recurrence behind the Hermite leading-term lemma. All exponents $\sigma\cup k$, $(\sigma\setminus k)\cup1^k$ are partitions in the sense of [[def-partition-young-diagram-and-conjugate-partition]].

With ell=m_1(sigma), that cycle must be selected from the k+ell fixed points of the product permutation, giving binom(k+ell,k)(k-1)!=(k+ell)!/(ell! k). The z-factor then gives coefficient k*m_k(sigma). Every other term has smaller Kerov degree, including the m_k=0 branch. items.title: The profile-moment generators in the shifted-character basis
items.statement:
Let $B(u):=1+\sum_{j\ge2}p_{j-1}^\#u^j$ be the formal power series with coefficients in $A$. Then for every $k\ge2$
$$\tilde p_k=[u^k]\bigl(B(u)^k\bigr)+\langle\text{terms of weight }\le k-1\rangle ,$$
the top weight component of $\tilde p_k$ being exactly the weight-$k$ component of the coefficient of $u^k$ in $B(u)^k$, on which $p_{k-1}^\#$ occurs with coefficient $k$. Consequently the linear functionals
$$L_k\bigl(p_\rho^\#\bigr):=\begin{cases}1,&k\ \text{even and}\ \rho=(1^{k/2}),\\0,&\text{otherwise,}\end{cases}$$
defined by linear extension on the full basis of $A$ (with $L_0(1)=1$), then restricted to weight-homogeneous elements of weight $k$, are multiplicative: if $f$ and $g$ are weight-homogeneous of weights $k'$ and $k-k'$, then $L_k(fg)=L_{k'}(f)L_{k-k'}(g)$; and
$$L_{2m}(\tilde p_{2m})=\binom{2m}{m},\qquad L_k(\tilde p_k)=0\ (k\ \text{odd}).$$

Lower canonical degree does not imply lower weight (p_1^# squared already demonstrates this), so the reader correctly removed that implication. Defining L_k on the full p^# basis avoids evaluating a functional only defined on homogeneous vectors at inhomogeneous basis elements. For a column output of weight k, deg_1<=weight forces both input partitions to be columns of their full allotted weights; the top coefficient is 1. items.title: Plancherel expectations of the shifted character observables
items.statement:
For every partition $\rho$ with $r=|\rho|$ and every $n\ge0$,
$$\mathbb E_{P_n}\bigl[p_\rho^\#\bigr]=\begin{cases}n^{\downarrow r},&\rho=(1^r),\\0,&\rho\ne(1^r),\end{cases}$$
where the case $n<r$ is included: then $p_\rho^\#\equiv0$ on $Y_n$ and $n^{\downarrow r}=0$. In particular $\mathbb E_{P_n}[p_\rho^\#]=O(n^{|\rho|})$ uniformly in $n$, and if $m_1(\rho)=0$ and $\rho\ne\emptyset$ then $\mathbb E_{P_n}[p_\rho^\#]=0$ for every $n$.
items.strategy:
For $n\ge r$ expand the expectation and use the definition of $p_\rho^\#$:
$$\mathbb E_{P_n}[p_\rho^\#]=\frac{n^{\downarrow r}}{n!}\sum_{\lambda\vdash n}\chi^\lambda\bigl(\rho\cup1^{n-r}\bigr)\,\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda .$$
By [[thm-finitely-many-irreducibles-occur-in-the-regular-representation-with-multiplicity-equal-to-their-degree]] the regular representation decomposes as $\mathbb C[S_n]\cong\bigoplus_{\lambda\vdash n}(S^\lambda)^{\oplus f^\lambda}$, so its character is $\chi_{\mathrm{reg}}=\sum_{\lambda}\dim(S^\lambda)\chi^\lambda$; by [[thm-character-of-the-regular-representation]] $\chi_{\mathrm{reg}}$ equals $n!$ at the identity class and $0$ on every other class. Hence the sum equals $n!$ precisely when the cycle type $\rho\cup1^{n-r}$ is the identity class $(1^n)$, that is, when $\rho=(1^r)$, and equals $0$ otherwise. Dividing by $n!$ and multiplying by $n^{\downarrow r}$ gives the claim; the case $n<r$ is the declared zero convention, consistent with $n^{\downarrow r}=0$. The bound and vanishing consequences are immediate. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Normalized shifted character observables $\eta_\rho$
items.statement:
Fix $n\ge1$. For a partition $\rho$ of [[def-shifted-character-observables-and-profile-moments]] write $|\rho|_1:=|\rho|+m_1(\rho)$, where $m_1(\rho)$ is the multiplicity of the part $1$. For $\lambda\vdash n$ with $n\ge|\rho|$ define the **normalized observable**
$$\eta_\rho^{(n)}(\lambda):=\frac{p_\rho^\#(\lambda)}{n^{|\rho|_1/2}\prod_{k\ge2}k^{m_k(\rho)/2}} .$$
For $n<|\rho|$ declare $\eta_\rho^{(n)}(\lambda):=0$, consistently with $p_\rho^\#(\lambda)=0$ there. Since $p_1^\#(\lambda)=n$, the definition can be written in the equivalent localized form
$$\eta_\rho^{(n)}=\frac{p_\rho^\#}{\bigl(p_1^\#\bigr)^{m_1(\rho)}\prod_{k\ge2}\bigl(k(p_1^\#)^k\bigr)^{m_k(\rho)/2}}\qquad\text{on }Y_n,$$
which is the concrete evaluation of the source's localization $A_{\mathrm{ext}}=A[(p_1^\#)^{1/2},(p_1^\#)^{-1/2}]$ on each $Y_n$; the equality uses $p_1^\#(\lambda)=n$, a positive number for $n\ge1$, so the square roots are ordinary positive real roots. In particular, for a single part $\rho=(k)$, $k\ge2$, one has $\eta_{(k)}^{(n)}=p_k^\#/(\sqrt k\,n^{k/2})=\eta_k^{(n)}$, the observable of [[def-joint-convergence-and-normalized-cycle-character-observables]].

Each $\eta_\rho^{(n)}$ is a real function on the finite set $Y_n$, hence a random variable on $(Y_n,P_n)$ ([[def-plancherel-measure-on-partitions]]), and for every $n\ge|\rho|$ the expectation of [[prop-plancherel-expectations-of-shifted-character-observables]] gives
$$\mathbb E_{P_n}\bigl[\eta_\rho^{(n)}\bigr]=\begin{cases}\dfrac{n^{\downarrow|\rho|}}{n^{|\rho|_1/2}\prod_{k\ge2}k^{m_k(\rho)/2}},&\rho=(1^{|\rho|}),\\[4pt]0,&\rho\ne(1^{|\rho|}),\end{cases}$$
so the expectation vanishes whenever $m_1(\rho)=0$ and $\rho\ne\emptyset$, and equals $\prod_{j=0}^{|\rho|-1}(1-j/n)\le1$ for $\rho=(1^{|\rho|})$; in every case it is $O(1)$ uniformly in $n$. Moreover
$$\bigl|\eta_\rho^{(n)}(\lambda)\bigr|\le n^{(|\rho|-m_1(\rho))/2}\prod_{k\ge2}k^{-m_k(\rho)/2}$$
for every $\lambda\vdash n$, $n\ge|\rho|$: by [[prop-basic-value-properties-of-a-complex-character]] every irreducible character satisfies $|\chi^\lambda_\mu|\le\chi^\lambda_{(1^n)}=\dim_{\mathbb C}S^\lambda$, so $|p_\rho^\#(\lambda)|\le n^{\downarrow|\rho|}\le n^{|\rho|}$, and dividing by $n^{|\rho|_1/2}\prod_{k\ge2}k^{m_k(\rho)/2}=n^{(|\rho|+m_1(\rho))/2}\prod_{k\ge2}k^{m_k(\rho)/2}$ gives the displayed bound. This normalization is the one used in [[lem-hermite-leading-terms-for-normalized-shifted-characters]] and [[thm-kerov-central-limit-theorem-for-normalized-cycle-characters]]. No choice principle is used.

items.title: Hermite leading terms for normalized shifted characters
items.statement:
For every partition $\rho$ with $m_1(\rho)=0$ and every $n\ge\max\{1,|\rho|\}$, the normalized observables satisfy
$$\prod_{k\ge2}H_{m_k(\rho)}\bigl(\eta_k^{(n)}\bigr)=\eta_\rho^{(n)}+R_\rho^{(n)}\qquad\text{on }Y_n,$$
where the remainder admits a finite expansion $R_\rho^{(n)}=\sum_{\sigma,j}c_{\sigma,j}\,n^{-j/2}\eta_\sigma^{(n)}$ with real constants $c_{\sigma,j}$ and $j\ge1$ such that the total degree $|\sigma|_1-j$ is strictly smaller than $|\rho|_1$, and $\sigma$ runs over partitions with $m_1(\sigma)=0$. Consequently
$$\Bigl|\mathbb E_{P_n}\Bigl[\prod_{k\ge2}H_{m_k(\rho)}(\eta_k^{(n)})\Bigr]-\mathbb E_{P_n}[\eta_\rho^{(n)}]\Bigr|=O\bigl(n^{-1/2}\bigr).$$
In particular, if $\rho\ne\emptyset$ then the expectation of the Hermite product is $O(n^{-1/2})$, and if $\rho=\emptyset$ it is $1$.

items.title: The monic probabilists' Hermite polynomials
items.statement:
The **monic probabilists' Hermite polynomials** are the polynomials $H_m\in\mathbb R[x]$ defined by
$$H_0=1,\qquad H_1(x)=x,\qquad xH_m(x)=H_{m+1}(x)+m\,H_{m-1}(x)\quad(m\ge1).$$
The recurrence is solved for the higher polynomial, $H_{m+1}(x)=xH_m(x)-mH_{m-1}(x)$, so it determines $H_m$ uniquely by induction on $m$. Each $H_m$ is monic of degree $m$: $H_2=x^2-1$, $H_3=x^3-3x$ and $H_4=x^4-6x^2+3$; in general $H_m(x)=m!\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor m/2\rfloor}\frac{(-1/2)^j x^{m-2j}}{j!\,(m-2j)!}$.

Under the AC assumption of the Gaussian-law supplier, these are the monic orthogonal polynomials for the standard normal law of [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]: they form an orthogonal system for the measure $(2\pi)^{-1/2}e^{-x^2/2}dx$; orthogonality and the expansion of monomials in this system are proved separately on this page. The moments of that law are those of [[def-moments-variance-and-covariance]], and the polynomial calculus used below is that of [[def-derivative]]. The defining property used in this batch is the recurrence; no choice principle is used.

items.statement: Assume AC. Then $X\sim N(0,1)$. More generally, let $Z$ be a real random variable with moment generating function finite on a neighbourhood of $0$, and set $m_k:=\mathbb E[Z^k]$. If $X$ has all absolute moments finite and $\mathbb E[X^k]=m_k$ for every $k\ge0$, then $X$ has the same law as $Z$.

items.title: The multivariate method of moments for a determinate limit
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, let $X_n$ be $\mathbb R^d$-valued random vectors with laws $\mu_n$, let $\mu$ be a Borel probability on $\mathbb R^d$ with all mixed moments finite, and suppose:

(i) for every multi-index $\alpha$, $\mathbb E[\prod_ix_i^{\alpha_i}]$ evaluated at $X_n$ converges to $\int\prod_ix_i^{\alpha_i}\,d\mu$;

(ii) $\mu$ is determined among Borel probabilities with finite moments by its mixed moments.

Then $\mu_n\Rightarrow\mu$ weakly. In particular every multivariate Gaussian law $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ is moment-determinate: a Borel probability with the same mixed moments as $N_d(m,\Sigma)$ equals it.

items.statement:
For $n\ge1$, let $\lambda$ range over $Y_n$ under the Plancherel measures $P_n$, let $\bar\lambda$ be the $\sqrt n$-scaled Russian profile of [[def-russian-profile-and-sqrt-n-scaling-of-a-young-diagram]], and let $\Omega$ be the limit profile of [[def-logan-shepp-vershik-kerov-limit-profile]]. Under the Plancherel measures $P_n$, for every integer $k\ge0$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R}\bigl(\bar\lambda(x)-\Omega(x)\bigr)x^k\,dx\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{in probability as }n\to\infty.$$
Equivalently, $\tilde p_j[\bar\lambda]\to\tilde p_j[\Omega]$ in probability for every $j\ge2$. Moreover, for every $f$ in the algebra $A=\mathbb R[\tilde p_2,\tilde p_3,\dots]$,
$$\mathbb E_{P_n}\bigl[f(\bar\lambda)\bigr]\longrightarrow f[\Omega].$$
items.strategy: In every generator monomial of weight k, the shifted-basis expansion uses only partitions of weight<=k. Regular-character expectations keep only columns (1^r); n^(-k/2)n^falling(r) tends to zero for 2r<k and to 1 for 2r=k, including constants. The previously verified L_k multiplicativity and central-binomial generator values identify this limit with evaluation at Omega. Applying it to tilde p_j and its square proves vanishing variance and convergence in probability by Chebyshev about the current mean. The exact multiplier 2/((k+1)(k+2)) transfers both directions between integral and profile-moment formulations, including k=0. All integrals are continuous and compactly supported for each finite diagram; uniform support is not required at this stage. IO Theorem 5.4 complete proof pp.27–28 agrees. The reader corrected the exact Proposition 2.2 locator to p.10; retained with no new item edit.

items.title: Plancherel Young diagrams converge to the limit shape
items.statement:
Let $\lambda$ range over $Y_n$ under the Plancherel measure $P_n$ and let $\bar\lambda$ be the $\sqrt n$-scaled Russian profile. Then
$$\sup_{x\in\mathbb R}\bigl|\bar\lambda(x)-\Omega(x)\bigr|\longrightarrow0\qquad\text{in probability as }n\to\infty.$$
items.strategy:
Let $C>e$ be fixed. By [[lem-rsk-union-bound-localizes-plancherel-profiles]] the event $E_n:=\{\lambda_1\le C\sqrt n,\ \lambda'_1\le C\sqrt n\}$ has $P_n(E_n)\to1$, and on $E_n$ the function $\sigma_{\bar\lambda}-\sigma_\Omega$ is supported in the fixed interval $I=[-C,C]$, is $1$-Lipschitz, and equals $\bar\lambda-|x|$ there. Given $\varepsilon>0$, apply [[lem-bounded-lipschitz-profile-moments-control-uniform-distance]] to $I$ with tolerance $\varepsilon/2$ to obtain $K$ and $\delta>0$ such that every $\sigma\in\Sigma_I$ whose first $K$ polynomial moments are at most $\delta$ in modulus satisfies $\sup|\sigma|\le\varepsilon/2$. Hence, on $E_n$, $\sup|\bar\lambda-\Omega|>\varepsilon$ forces $\sup|\sigma_{\bar\lambda}-\sigma_\Omega|>\varepsilon/2$ and therefore $|\int(\bar\lambda-\Omega)x^kdx|>2\delta$ for some $0\le k\le K$, so
$$\bigl\{\sup_x|\bar\lambda-\Omega|>\varepsilon\bigr\}\subseteq E_n^c\cup\bigcup_{k=0}^{K}\Bigl\{\bigl|\int(\bar\lambda-\Omega)x^kdx\bigr|>2\delta\Bigr\},$$
using that $\bar\lambda-\Omega$ vanishes outside $I$ on $E_n$ and that $\sigma_{\bar\lambda}-\sigma_\Omega=\tfrac12(\bar\lambda-\Omega)$ is $1$-Lipschitz and supported in $I$ on $E_n$: on $x>0$ both $\sigma_{\bar\lambda}$ and $\sigma_\Omega$ are nonincreasing and $1$-Lipschitz, on $x<0$ both are nondecreasing and $1$-Lipschitz, the two pieces agree at $0$, and subtracting a monotone $1$-Lipschitz function from another preserves the $1$-Lipschitz bound; the lemma is applied to $\sigma_{\bar\lambda}-\sigma_\Omega$ and $\sup|\bar\lambda-\Omega|=2\sup|\sigma_{\bar\lambda}-\sigma_\Omega|$. Each of the finitely many moment events has probability tending to $0$ by [[prop-scaled-plancherel-profile-moments-converge-in-probability]], and $P_n(E_n^c)\to0$; subadditivity ([[lem-probability-measure-basic-identities]]) gives the claim for this $\varepsilon$, and $\varepsilon>0$ is arbitrary. This is the source's Theorem 5.5, with the local RSK union bound replacing Hammersley's theorem for Lemma 5.6. No choice principle is used in the estimates (the finite-dimensional Euclidean computations are explicit).

items.title: Kerov's central limit theorem for normalized cycle characters
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). For every fixed integer $N\ge2$, as $n\to\infty$ under the Plancherel measures $P_n$,
$$\bigl(\eta_k^{(n)}\bigr)_{2\le k\le N}\ \Longrightarrow\ N_{N-1}(0,I_{N-1}),$$
that is, the $N-1$ normalized cycle-character observables of [[def-joint-convergence-and-normalized-cycle-character-observables]] converge jointly in distribution to independent standard Gaussians. Equivalently,
$$\Bigl(\frac{p_k^\#}{n^{k/2}}\Bigr)_{2\le k\le N}\ \Longrightarrow\ (\zeta_2,\dots,\zeta_N),$$
where the $\zeta_k$ are independent centered Gaussians of variances $k$. Convergence is the joint convergence of [[def-joint-convergence-and-normalized-cycle-character-observables]].
items.strategy: Every fixed Hermite multi-index defines a no-one partition rho; the empty tuple has expectation exactly 1, and every other tuple has expectation O(n^(-1/2)) by the independently reviewed leading-term and regular-character suppliers. Gaussian independence and integrable polynomial factors give the same limiting Hermite moments. The finite monomial/Hermite change of basis yields all mixed moments, and the corrected multivariate moment theorem applies in dimension N-1>=1 with a determinate Gaussian target. Coordinate rescaling gives independent variances k for the unnormalized form. Fixed N is essential; no infinite-vector topology or edge limit is claimed. IO Theorem 6.1 and its full proof pp.29–32 agree. Read Sniady Theorem/Definition 3.1 p.10, Theorem 3.2 p.11, Corollary 3.3 and full proof pp.11–12, Example 3.4 p.13: these support the alternative citation but are not needed for local closure. Amended F1 to n>=max(1,|rho|), matching the positive-order supplier even at rho empty, and refreshed the contract's normalization quotation after the inverse-square-root repair. AC is declared at all Gaussian and moment-method uses.

items.title: The RSK and longest-increasing-subsequence consequences remain owned by the hook-length/RSK page
items.statement: This page consumes the distribution of the Robinson-Schensted shape of a uniform permutation ([[thm-rsk-shape-of-a-uniform-random-permutation-has-plancherel-law]]) and Schensted's longest increasing and decreasing subsequence theorem only to localize Plancherel profiles ([[lem-rsk-union-bound-localizes-plancherel-profiles]]). It does not re-mint RSK, the LIS/LDS identities, the Baik-Deift-Johansson theorem, the Tracy-Widom distribution, determinantal point processes or edge statistics of Plancherel measure: those belong to the hook-length/RSK page and to separate analytic-probability suppliers, and the limit-shape theorem proved here ([[thm-plancherel-young-diagrams-converge-to-the-limit-shape]]) is the qualitative law of large numbers, not a fluctuation or edge result. In particular no sharp constant, rate or fluctuation-distribution statement is asserted: the localization lemma gives only the bound $\lambda_1,\lambda'_1\le C\sqrt n$ with probability tending to one, for each fixed $C>e$, and the limit-shape theorem gives only convergence in probability of the scaled profile to $\Omega$.
items.strategy: The remark accurately limits this page to the proved finite shape law, C>e localization and qualitative uniform-profile LLN. None of these supplies a Tracy–Widom or edge-fluctuation law, and the remark asserts none. Its reader-repaired bibliography distinguishes Romik Chapter 2 (fluctuations beginning p.79 and edge statistics beginning p.143) from §§1.18–1.20 (dimensions, growth, and final shape theorem pp.62–70). items.title: The Plancherel measure on partitions of three
items.statement:
For $n=3$ the partitions are $(3)$, $(2,1)$ and $(1^3)$, with $f^{(3)}=f^{(1^3)}=1$ and $f^{(2,1)}=2$; hence
$$P_3(3)=P_3(1^3)=\frac{1}{6},\qquad P_3(2,1)=\frac{4}{6}=\frac23,$$
and $\tfrac16+\tfrac46+\tfrac16=1$, recovering [[prop-plancherel-weights-sum-to-one]] in the smallest non-uniform case.
items.strategy:
Verification: enumerate the standard tableaux of the three shapes. For $(3)$ the increasing row $\boxed{1\,2\,3}$ is the only standard tableau; for $(1^3)$ the increasing column is the only one; for $(2,1)$ there are exactly two,
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline1&2\\\hline3\end{array}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline1&3\\\hline2\end{array},$$
so $f^{(3)}=1$, $f^{(2,1)}=2$, $f^{(1^3)}=1$ (also obtainable from the hook-length formula: $3!/(3\cdot2\cdot1)=1$, $3!/(3\cdot1\cdot1)=2$, $3!/(3\cdot2\cdot1)=1$). Squaring and dividing by $3!=6$ gives the stated weights; the sum is $6/6=1$. Every step is a finite count. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The RSK shapes of the six permutations of $S_3$
items.statement:
Running Robinson-Schensted row insertion on the six permutations of $\{1,2,3\}$ gives
$$123\mapsto(3),\quad 132\mapsto(2,1),\quad 213\mapsto(2,1),\quad 231\mapsto(2,1),\quad 312\mapsto(2,1),\quad 321\mapsto(1^3);$$
the resulting shape frequencies are $\tfrac16$ for $(3)$, $\tfrac46$ for $(2,1)$ and $\tfrac16$ for $(1^3)$, matching $P_3$ of [[ex-plancherel-measure-on-partitions-of-three]] and confirming [[thm-rsk-shape-of-a-uniform-random-permutation-has-plancherel-law]] at $n=3$.
items.strategy: Verification by explicit insertion ([[def-row-insertion-and-bumping-route]]): $123$ fills one row $(3)$; $132$: insert $1$, then $3$, then $2$ bumps $3$ to the second row, giving shape $(2,1)$; $213$: $2$, then $1$ bumps $2$, then $3$ gives $(2,1)$; $231$: $2,3$, then $1$ bumps $2$, giving $(2,1)$; $312$: $3$, then $1$ bumps $3$, then $2$ gives $(2,1)$; $321$: $3$, then $2$ bumps $3$, then $1$ bumps $2$, giving the column $(1^3)$. Recording tableaux confirm the pairs are distinct ([[thm-robinson-schensted-correspondence]]). Counting the shapes gives the displayed frequencies. No choice principle is used.

items.title: The Plancherel measure is not uniform on partitions
items.statement: For every $n\ge3$, the Plancherel measure on $Y_n$ is uniform on the partitions of $n$.
items.strategy: The Statement refuted now asserts uniformity, while the title and counterexample correctly assert its failure. Direct hook-length computation gives dimensions 1 for (n) and n-1 for (n-1,1), hence distinct weights for every n>=3; at n=3 they are 1/6,4/6,1/6. The n>=3 restriction is essential (n<=2 has uniform weights). The reader's correction of the false-statement/witness labeling is retained; no unnecessary witness edit.
